stories.title: Trump’s Next War? Leaked Plans Reveal Escalation in Cuba and Iran
stories.text: From leaked reports showing the U.S. Army preparing potential options around Cuba to the U.S. Navy’s strategic tactical shift away from the Iranian blockade line, Murtaza Hussain and Sarmad Jawad analyze what’s driving these moves—and what Trump’s post-midterm foreign policy strategy could look like. Plus, a look into Iran’s updated terminal guidance missile capabilities, the human toll aboard US naval deployments, and how $100+ oil prices are shaping negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz. Then a deep dive into the rise of China in the Trump era as Xi Jinping pays a state visit for the first time in 10 years. Drop Site News is an independent news outlet covering war and politics.

stories.title: Massacre at Minab: The School That Became a Grave
stories.text: Illustration: Images drawn by Fatemeh Zahra Bahrami, a child who survived the school bombing at Minab, provided to Drop Site. In the background, the cemetery where the victims are buried. On the morning of Saturday, February 28, people across Iran began their day like any other. It was one week into the Islamic holy month of Ramadan, and people were preparing for their work and school week. Parents hustled their children out the door for school as the notorious morning traffic jams filled the streets of Tehran and other cities. In the southern Iranian city of Minab, preschool teacher Hossniyeh Salem was getting ready to leave the house. “Like any other day, I got my child ready at 7 o’clock—because my son is in fifth grade and attended the same school,” she recalled. “I got Yassin ready and headed to school. Yassin went to the boys’ school and I stayed at preschool, in my own class.” It was Salem’s seventh year as a teacher at Shajareh Tayyebeh, a well-respected, private school. “The upper floor was for girls and the downstairs was for boys. stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: Watch Trump's new chatbot debunk his lies
stories.text: “Instead of forcing citizens to search through the endless maze of tens of thousands of terrible government websites and rules and more than 10,000 forms,” Trump said, Americans will visit America.gov. That is the vision, but currently, America.gov is not integrated with the services of federal agencies. At Tuesday’s event, Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to facilitate integration in the future. Whether and when it will actually function as advertised is an open question. Right now, America.gov functions as an AI chatbot that bases its answers on official government sources. “Simply ask for what you need and America.gov will provide answers and it will be provided immediately,” Trump said. “Anyone who has used Grok or Gemini or ChatGPT will understand instantly how to use America.gov.” It was developed with the assistance of Google’s Gemini and SpaceXAI’s Grok , according to Joe Gebbia, the Airbnb co-founder who led development of the site for the Trump administration. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: The Global Shell Game Hiding Forever Chemicals
stories.text: This story was published in collaboration with the Investigative Reporting Lab at Yale . I grew up walking the boardwalk in downtown Wilmington, North Carolina, peering into the froth of the Cape Fear River. The name came from 16th-century mariners who feared its mouth, which was known to churn ships into wrecks. But for the last few decades, there has been something new to fear in the river. The Cape Fear River was tainted with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), the Wilmington Star-News reported in 2017, a group of synthetic compounds now commonly known as “forever chemicals.” As their name suggests, forever chemicals are renowned for their persistence. One of the strongest bonds in chemistry, carbon and fluorine, gives PFAS their nonstick properties. A seemingly endless list of products — dental floss, tampons, cellphones, wall paint, yoga pants, carpets, contact lenses, hair-straightening treatments, toilet paper — rely on those bonds to smooth, harden, slicken, and withstand heat and wear. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: The Financial System Can’t Afford To Treat You Fairly
stories.text: We all sense that the American economy is one big con game, in which we’re the mark. But one of the world’s largest Wall Street firms just accidentally confessed that truth in a warning to the investor class. The admission came from Apollo Global Management’s chief economist in a web post summarizing the potential macroeconomic effects of personal AI agents that can assist people with day-to-day tasks. It warned the financial class that AI agents could trigger a bank run, evoking a mashup of The Terminator and It’s a Wonderful Life . Think a legion of T-1000s lined up at George Bailey’s teller window in Bedford Falls . But if you read past the headline, you’ll see that the revelation is about a far different kind of bank run. In this projected scenario, AI agents help Americans flee the banks swindling them with low interest payments on their deposits — a prospect which Apollo says could destabilize the entire financial system. That latter conclusion is an inadvertent — and exceedingly rare — acknowledgement that yes, the financial system literally relies on the continued systematic fleecing of bank customers. The good news is that we could actually do a lot to halt this mass theft

stories.author: Drop Site team
stories.title: Two Oil Tankers Freed From Pirates Off the Coast of Somalia
stories.text: MOGADISHU, Somalia—The maritime force for Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland region has seized control of two separate hijacked oil tankers, Puntland security sources tell Drop Site News. Honour 25, which was hijacked by Somali pirates in late April was initially carrying 18,500 barrels of oil (worth an estimated $1.7 million), while MT Eureka seized in May was initially carrying 20,400 barrels of diesel (worth an estimated $4.3 million). The Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF)—created in 2013 with funding from the United Arab Emirates and trained by private South African security firm Saransor—is tasked with maritime security and anti-piracy operations in Somali territorial waters that fall under Puntland’s jurisdiction. A statement released today by the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) stated that, when it regained “control” of Honour 25, five members of the crew had been killed—deaths they attributed to pirates—and four wounded during the operation. The rest of the crew was rescued safely. stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: How MAGA Inc. raised so much money
stories.text: Trump has made it clear that he has complete authority over the funds, although such direct control is prohibited by law. “This is money from MAGA Inc. This is my money that I control,” Trump said. “I can spend it for what I want to spend it for.” The amount raised by Trump’s super PAC is unprecedented. It is a larger war chest than any entity has ever had to spend in a midterm election. Super PACs supporting former President Joe Biden, for example, raised $57 million in the year after his election . (Biden was also eligible to run again in 2024.) So how is Trump raising so much money? Sarofim is the founder and CEO of Trousdale Ventures, a venture capital firm. (Sarofim previously donated $1 million to Trump’s inaugural committee, according to the New York Times .) Sarofim’s Trousdale Ventures is a major investor in CesiumAstro, which makes communications systems for satellites. Trousdale Ventures has led multiple rounds of financing for the company. CesiumAstro is listed under Sarofim’s “Notable Deals” on his company bio .
